messages:
emily-csm: FYI Orion (mid-market, onboarding) just asked to shorten renewal to 10 months and drop seats from 120->100. Theywant a 12% discount and insist billing to UK entity (Orion Ltd). Procurement says they will send a PO but want the SOW updated with prorated fees and a wet signature. Can Legal/Finance weigh in?
ana-sales: yikes on 12% — thatis steep. From ARR perspective weprefer keeping 12mo and full seat count but we can be flexible. Can we offer a smaller discount + onboarding milestone credit to keep ARR intact?
kevin-csm: context: theyhavent hit baseline usage yet; onboarding delays are the reason they want shorter term. If we tie part of the discount to hitting enablement milestones that should protect us. Also need clear seat true-up and reporting cadence.
linda-legal: wet signature for UK entity is sometimes requested. We prefer DocuSign for speed and audit trail. If they require wet we can accept but need a guarantor/parent signature and add clause about execution timing. Will also draft SOW language for seat counts + prorate.
jarod-finance: vendor code & invoicing: must have billing entity, VAT GB987654, PO number, invoice email. For shortened term we want net30; if client insists net60 require 50% upfront. Also finance prefers discount tied to performance (usage or milestone).
billing-bot: Reminder: update opportunity in CRM: add payment term flag + vendor entity before generating invoice template.
ana-sales: suggested commercial: offer 8% discount + one-time onboarding credit equal to 1 month of expected usage (applied to first invoice) and keep 10mo term + seat change. Condition: signed amendment + PO referencing invoice match. That keeps revenue near target. Thoughts?
emily-csm: That seems reasonable. I'll propose it to procurement and explain the milestone credit. Also ask if UK parent can sign via DocuSign as guarantor to avoid wet.
linda-legal: I'll prepare an amendment draft with two signature flows: (1) preferred: DocuSign by UK parent as guarantor + DocuSign by UK entity if possible; (2) fallback: wet-sign for UK entity + guarantor clause. Also SOW with prorate table and seat true-up quarterly.
jarod-finance: fine with 8% + 1-month credit if contract includes a true-up and payment terms net30. We'll only issue vendor code after legal confirms executed contract. If PO says net60, require 50% upfront as exception.
kevin-csm: I'll prepare the usage projection + two invoice examples (with and without overage) to show procurement. That usually helps acceptance.
ana-sales: can we also add early-termination protection? i.e., if they terminate early we reclaim prorated credits and any unused onboarding credit. Simple clause.
linda-legal: yes I'll include an early termination recoup clause and a clause that credits are forfeited if payment terms are violated.
emily-csm: action items: @linda-legal draft amendment (include both signature paths) by EOD; @jarod-finance prepare vendor-code checklist after legal sign; @kevin-csm produce invoice examples; @ana-sales lead negotiation. I'll ping procurement this afternoon.
emily-csm: Update 24h later: procurement replied — they will accept DocuSign if parent signs as guarantor. PO number sample: PO-2026-OR-3344. They requested net60 but agreed to 50% upfront as a condition. Procurement to send final PO tomorrow.
linda-legal: Draft posted in thread (link). Amendment includes: 8% discount, 1-month credit applied to first invoice, 10mo term, seat adjustment to 100 with quarterly true-up, overage at $0.0005/token, early termination recoup. Two signature flows included.
arid-not-a-real-user: (note: internal) Please do not post PHI.
emily-csm: Thanks team — I'll attach the draft to the opportunity and confirm PO when received. Rolling to close once DocuSign returns signed.
